name: Orpheus
from: Idea 2 with some of Idea 3: an RPG Maker game after Orpheus, losing autonomy step by step, with Stanley Parable-style choices.
hook: The guide will get you both out. It only asks to choose the doors.
pitch: Orpheus leads Eurydice through five rooms out of the underworld. A helpful guide offers to choose for you, and each room it chooses more; your options grey out. By the last room the only choice left is the old one: whether to look back.
minute_check: Yes, for anyone who knows the myth; the guide’s first line covers the rest.
build_check: Yes in RPG Maker with five rooms.
scope: Five rooms. Write the guide’s lines for each room first; they are the antagonist and the helper.

brief.player: Orpheus, leading Eurydice out of the underworld.
brief.goal: Reach the surface without looking back.
brief.ending: The guide that helps you (the AI) makes more choices for you each room. Whether you look back is the only choice left; the ending depends on it.
brief.verb: Walk, and choose (fewer options each room).
brief.theme: Autonomy lost a step at a time, to a guide that is not simply bad. You asked for the help.
brief.look: Muted 3D-looking office spaces like The Stanley Parable, in an underworld.

prov.bug: The guide picks the doors. Much faster!
prov.nit: When the guide chooses, can the player see what it chose against?

refs_lit: The source: Orpheus looks back. Decide whether your player can be made to.
Your own reference: choice everywhere but meaningless.
A recent retelling where Orpheus is a character; useful for how myth carries into play.
omni_gameplay_prompt: Atmospheric top-down 2.5D mythological office-underworld adventure in muted charcoal (#22252a), warm bone (#e6e1d3), and antique gold (#d9b45a). Smooth overhead tracking camera. Orpheus walks ahead of a pale trailing Eurydice through stark Stanley-Parable-like subterranean corridors; at each branching doorway, a golden AI guide beam automatically seals and greys out two doors, steering them forward while Orpheus resists turning around toward the footsteps behind him. Continuous unbroken gameplay shot, no scene cuts, no HUD text. Use the reference image for palette and corridor staging. Sound design: echoing footsteps, quiet harp notes mixed with fluorescent office hum. No dialogue.
